newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss, Jewish group make progress on Holocaust fund.
newsitem.headline: Swiss, Jewish group make progress on Holocaust fund.

text.p: Swiss and Jewish negotiators are making progress in talks on how to run a Holocaust memorial fund financed with contributions from Swiss banks, a senior World Jewish Congress (WJC) official said.
WJC Assistant Secretary General Maram Stern said after a round of talks on Monday night that his group, which has led a campaign for the fund, saw no big problems over who will run it.
"This will be quickly done. We are going to do this (Tuesday) morning," he said.

But he suggested the memorial fund, which Berne intends to set up quickly with contributions from private businesses, should be combined with a broader humanitarian foundation the government has proposed and which would draw on federal funds.
The public foundation must await the first findings later this year of a historians' panel now reviewing Switzerland's wartime role as a financial centre, the government has said.

Berne will then decide what steps may be appropriate to make amends for Switzerland's economic collaboration with Nazi Germany and its anti-Jewish wartime immigration policy that turned back thousands of Jewish refugees as the Holocaust raged.
"I presented another view that there should be one (fund) that does everything. I don't like...stretching it out. One would be nicer than two," Stern told Reuters.
Big Swiss banks have already contributed 100 million Swiss francs ($68.5 million) to the fund, and other businesses have pledged to follow suit.

Officials close to the talks also said they believed priority for the money would go to Jews and other Holocaust survivors in eastern Europe, who were cut off for decades from earlier compensation programs by the former Iron Curtain.

The officials said the WJC had no objection to sharing the proceeds with non-Jewish victims of the Holocaust, including gypsies, whose organisation for Switzerland was due to be represented at the Tuesday talks.
Swiss banks were set to join the negotiations on Tuesday.

Swiss Foreign Minister Flavio Cotti met WJC Secretary General Israel Singer in Berne on Monday, two weeks after the government and major Jewish groups agreed to put aside months of quarrelling and cooperate in compensating Holocaust victims.

The WJC has campaigned since 1995 for compensation from Switzerland along two lines -- from Swiss banks for keeping the accounts of Jews killed in the Holocaust and from the country as a whole for profiting cynically from business with Nazi Germany.
